1    Q. Please state your name and address.

2    A. David Rosenkranz. My address is 12927 Romberg Road Holland, Texas 76534

3    Q. Are you the same David Rosenkranz who filed a Motion to Intervene in this

4    proceeding?

5    A. Yes. PUC Docket Number 59475, link# D11 Track # 3070. Motion to Intervene #267.

6    Q. Please state your background.

7    A. We are the landowners I am Retired. I spent 45 years working in high tech.

8    Q. Are you testifying on behalf of the above-listed landowner?

9    A. Yes

10   Q. Is the property affected by the 765kv transmission line project proposed by

11   Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC?

12   A. Yes The center line of Link D11 will be routed within approx. 405 feet of our home.

13   Q. What is the purpose of your testimony?

14   A. We oppose link D11.

15   Q. What are the routes on this property?

16   A. 296, 304, 706, 739, 910, 911, 913, 914, 915, 916, 1189, 1193, 1203, 1217, 1219.

2   Q. Have the pictures been altered?

3   A. No

4   Q. Do the pictures accurately represent the views of the property?

5   A. Yes

6   Q. Description of the property?

7   A. The property is 14.431 acres located in Bell County, Texas, identified as tract No.

8   3070 in the application materials. The property has our home a 4 bedroom two bath
                                Direct Testimony of {David Rosenkranz and Barbara Wright-Rosenkranz}
                                                                              PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                      SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                       Page 12 of 20
 1    house that we built with our own hands as part of our retirement strategy. It also has

2    four out buildings (all have metal roofs, 3 are metal buildings with metal roofs) including

3    a workshop all less than 300 feet of the transmission lines and a pole barn

4    approximately 200 feet from the lines. We are also under a wildlife AG exemption and

5    have spent a lot of time and effort to provide a safe habitat for wildlife. The surrounding

6    landscape is mainly rural and agricultural, with single dwelling homesteads.

7    Q. Approximately where is your location in the study area?

8    A. In Bell County Texas On link D11 tract# 3070.

                             LAND USE, CONCERNS AND HISTORY

9    Q. Please give a brief history of the property and your association with it.

10   A. We moved to the property in 1988 when there was nothing out here. We planted over

11   50 pecan trees and many other variety of trees and plants and dug a pond (stock tank)

12   and turned the property into a sanctuary for all kinds of wildlife and native grasses and

13   flowers. We also built our house and multiple outbuildings, ourselves me, my wife, kids

14   and in-laws. We have 5 buildings all with metal roofs, and 3 are metal buildings, (our

15   home has a metal roof). Through substantial investment of both monetary and sweat

16   equity we have transformed a vacant field into a country homestead with country views

17   and a sanctuary for wildlife. The thought of a 765 kv steel lattice tower standing up to

18   198 feet tall being erected within 300 feet of our home is an abomination.

19   Q. Please describe how the property is used today and how this transmission line

20   may affect that use.
                                 Direct Testimony of {David Rosenkranz and Barbara Wright-Rosenkranz}
                                                                               PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                       SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                        Page 13 of 20
 1    A. The property is where we live this is our homestead and we also have a wildlife AG

2    exemption. The transmission lines will be right out our back door approximately 300 feet

3    and much closer to our barn. It will destroy our view from the back yard and corona hum

4    will be so loud that we will not be able to enjoy time in our swimming pool. We feel that

5    the noise from the lines and the EMF will drive away all the pollinators that feed on the

6    native grasses and flowers and the wildlife will no longer find refuge on our property.

7    The proposed Link D11, if constructed as proposed, would permanently damage the

8    property in the following ways: (1) the presence of towers and conductors within 300

9    feet of our home would wipe out our investment in our retirement strategy. (2) Increased

10   wildfire risk, (3) corona hum noise pollution, (4) Migratory fowl collisions, (5) ground

11   nesting birds habitat disruption and declining native songbirds. Our home is marked as

12   "Habitable Structure 84" in the Oncor permit application. The ATT-Habitable Structures

13   document indicates it is 405 feet from the center line. The proposed 765 kV

14   transmission line, if built on link D11, would place steel lattice towers standing between

15   155 and 198 feet in height, 141 feet 8 inches wide within a 200-foot right-of-way

16   corridor. The ROW edge will be 305 feet from our home. In addition, the ROW edge of

17   Link D11 will be less than 300 feet from all our out buildings and less than 200 feet from

18   our barn. We oppose link D11 and respectively request the rejection or modification of

19   the routes associated with proposed Link D11 route because it affects my family's Bell

20   County property and to identify a more suitable route that avoids close proximity to our

21   home.




                                  Direct Testimony of {David Rosenkranz and Barbara Wright-Rosenkranz}
                                                                                PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                        SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                         Page 14 of 20
 1    Q. What types of concerns do you have with regard to the transmission line

2    segments and routes proposed?

3    A. Although I am not a medical doctor we have health concerns about being so close to

4    765 kv lines. We also have concerns about lighting strikes and wildfires.

                                        FINANCIAL RISKS

5    Q. What do you think the financial risks will be to you?

6    A. The financial risks to my family are severe and likely permanent. Our home and land

7    represents the primary asset of our family. The placement of a 765 kV transmission line

8    with towers up to 198 feet tall within 300 feet of our home will destroy the market value

9    of our residential property. A 765 kV line, the highest voltage class in common use,

10   located on the doorstep of our home represents a worst-case scenario for property

11   value.

12   Q. What are the risks of devaluation of your property?

13   A. The risk of devaluation of our property is very high, as stated above the value of our

14   home will be reduced. The visual and audible presence of the transmission lines

15   diminishes the rural character and aesthetic value of rural land. The application

16   documents acknowledge that construction of the proposed project creates permanent

17   aesthetic impacts and that transmission structures and wires will be permanently visible.

18   A 200-foot ROW within 300 feet of our home eliminates any reasonable expectation of

19   market recovery for our home and land.

                      HEALTH RISKS, ENVIRONMENTAL AND WILDLIFE
                                 Direct Testimony of {David Rosenkranz and Barbara Wright-Rosenkranz}
                                                                               PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                       SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                        Page 15 of 20
 1    Q. What do you think are the health risks?

2    A. We are extremely concerned about the health risks of living within 300 feet of an

3    energized 765 kV transmission line. This is our retirement home and our children and

4    grandchildren come to visit, and their health and safety is a great concern of ours and

5    one day it will be their inheritance. At 765 kv this line will generate extremely low

6    frequency (ELF) electromagnetic fields (EMF) with intensities that are among the

7    highest associated with any overhead transmission line in common use.

8    Q. What do you see as safety risks?

9    A. The safety risks of living within 300 feet of a 765 kV line could be very substantial.

10   First, Bell County experiences significant severe weather events including tornadoes

11   and high winds. A tower failure or collapse or conductor break from severe weather

12   within feet of our home could be deadly. Second, the towers themselves attract lightning

13   strikes and create a risk for wildfires. We have a wildlife AG exemption on our property

14   and we allow the native grasses and wildflowers to grow for the wildlife which posses an

15   increased risk to our home and property in the event of a wildfire started by a lightning

16   strike.

17   Q. What do you think will be the environmental impacts and risks?

18   A. Land erosion. The proposed TOWERS will cross the major drainage water way, as

19   our land sits between 3 ridges, east, south, west, and drains north to creeks and tanks

20   and ponds. This tower would impede historical drainage and impede water flow, as our

21   land becomes rivers in heavy rains. And, increased risk of lightning strikes and wildfires,

                                  Direct Testimony of {David Rosenkranz and Barbara Wright-Rosenkranz}
                                                                                PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                        SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                         Page 16 of 20
 1    wind noise blowing across the lines and lattice towers. The destruction of the view and

2    skyline and the peacefulness of country life.

3    Q. What do you think will be the risks to birds and native wildlife?

4    A. We have a fence line with a row of thick trees approximately 25 plus feet deep that

5    are just a few feet away from the proposed transmission lines. On our property we have

6    seen the Protected Species Hawks, owls, a bald eagle, two golden eagles and a lot of

7    migratory birds that rest and nest in those trees. We have seen a lot of Monarch

8    butterflies on our property during migration. I have twice seen the Threatened Species

9    the Texas Horned Lizard, we have seen cranes, herons and egrets stop at our stock

10   tank. We have seen bob white quail, road runners, kill deer, white tail deer and a lot of

11   other migratory animals and birds stop at our stock tank and live in our brush pile

12   habitats and use our tree lines as migratory corridors and thickets for cover. We feel that

13   these lines will deter the wildlife and (particularly pollinators on which the entire food

14   chain rely on), from visiting and living on our property.

15   Q. What do you think will be the risks to your agricultural activities and animals?

16   A. We have a wildlife AG exemption. It is our belief that the HIGHEST POSSIBLE

17   VOLTAGES will drive off all the pollinators and wildlife we have worked to provide a safe

18   habitat for.

19   Q. What do you think will be the risks to your stock tanks and ground water?

20   A. We have not had the time to research the impact because of our shortened less than

21   30 days to respond.
                                  Direct Testimony of {David Rosenkranz and Barbara Wright-Rosenkranz}
                                                                                PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                        SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                         Page 17 of 20
                     RECREATION, COMMUNITY VALUES AND AESTHETICS

1    Q. How would this transmission line affect your enjoyment of your property?

2    A. It would destroy our enjoyment we would have health concerns about being outside

3    for extended periods of time. We would probably no longer use and enjoy our

4    swimming pool because of the health concerns with exposure to the EMF at that close

5    range. It would destroy our view when we walk out our backdoor. It would limit any

6    further construction of out buildings behind our house because they would be less than

7    300 feet from the lines. We use the back section of our property for clay pigeon (target)

8    shooting, this will affect that activity for fear of hitting a tower or power line.

9    Q. Do you think the proposed transmission line will affect any planned future use

10   on your land?

11   A. Yes, we are planning on converting one of our out buildings into a cottage for our

12   children and grandchildren. But it will be too close to the lines.

13   Q. How would this transmission line affect your rural community values for your

14   area?

15   A. It will negatively affect our community values. All property values within eyesight of

16   these massive 198 foot tall towers will be negatively affected. It would destroy our

17   scenic views and the serenity of country life and change the landscape into an industrial

18   corridor.

19   Q. How will this transmission line affect the aesthetic value of your property?


                                   Direct Testimony of {David Rosenkranz and Barbara Wright-Rosenkranz}
                                                                                 PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                         SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                          Page 18 of 20
 1    A. It will have a negative affect on the aesthetic value of our property, as soon as you

2    walk out the back door they will hit you in the face with tall 198 foot towers and line

3    buzzing. We have approximately 45 to 50 pecans trees and spending time outside on

4    our property is very relaxing and appealing that will all be destroyed by these lines.

5    Q. Do transmission routes parallel any existing rights of way on your property?

6    A. We have high voltage lines running on the front of our property and these will run

7    adjacent to the back of our property line. Our house will be trapped between two high

8    voltage lines a double burden financially and safety wise.

9    Q. Does Oncor’s application properly identify the structures on your property?

10   A. The aerial view showed all the buildings. But no where did it say that our barn was

11   less than 200 feet from the ROW and our three other out buildings where less than 300

12   feet. It just mentioned our house was 300 feet from the ROW.




                          LOCAL ELECTRICITY SERVICE AND COSTS.

13   Q. Do you think that this transmission line will improve your electric service in

14   your area?

15   A. Not at all, they are going to supply power to the Permian basin, they are of no benefit

16   to the residents of Bell County.

17   Q. Do you think this transmission line will lower your electricity costs?
                                  Direct Testimony of {David Rosenkranz and Barbara Wright-Rosenkranz}
                                                                                PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                        SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                         Page 19 of 20
 1    A. Not at all.

2                          CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATION

3    Q: Is there anything else you would like to have considered in this proceeding?

4    A. Yes if this project is intended for future economic development in the Permian Basin,

5    then instead of taking power from Bell County and jeopardizing our grid in Bell County

6    during peak usage ERCOT should look into localized power generation where it is

7    needed in the Permian Basin. This will also limit the people affected by a power outage

8    if the power is generated locally where it is needed. It is my opinion that the only way to

9    stabilize the grid is to add more power generating capability. Why should the land

10   owners, farmers, ranchers, small homesteads and families that live on property affected

11   by these lines or close to these lines pay the price.

12   Q. Does the conclude your testimony?

13   A. Yes, at present it does, but I reserve the right to amend or supplement my testimony.

14   I respectfully request that the Commission give full and serious consideration to the

15   harms I have described, and that it require the applicants to develop and adopt an

16   alternative route for the Bell County portion of the project that does not place a 765 kV

17   transmission line within close proximity to my family's home.




                                 Direct Testimony of {David Rosenkranz and Barbara Wright-Rosenkranz}
                                                                               PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                       SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                        Page 20 of 20

11   value.

  1   Q. What do you think are the health risks?


 2   A. We are extremely concerned about the health risks of living within 300 feet of an

 3   energized 765 kV transmission line. This is our retirement home and our children and

 5   one day it will be their inheritance. At 765 kv this line will generate extremely low

 6   frequency (ELF) electromagnetic fields (EMF) with intensities that are among the

 7   highest associated with any overhead transmission line in common use.

13   strikes and create a risk for wildfires. We have a wildlife AG exemption on our property

14   and we allow the native grasses and wildflowers to grow for the wildlife which posses an

15   increased risk to our home and property in the event of a wildfire started by a lightning

16   strike.

21   land becomes rivers in heavy rains. And, increased risk of lightning strikes and wildfires,

 2                         CONCLUSIONSAND RECOMMENDATION

 3   Q: Is there anything else you would like to have considered in this proceeding?


 4   A. Yes if this project is intended for future economic development in the Permian Basin,

 5   then instead of taking power from Bell County and jeopardizing our grid in Bell County

 6   during peak usage ERCOT should look into localized power generation where it is

 7   needed in the Permian Basin. This will also limit the people affected by a power outage

 8   if the power is generated locally where it is needed. It is my opinion that the only way to

 9   stabilize the grid is to add more power generating capability. Why should the land

10   owners, farmers, ranchers, small homesteads and families that live on property affected

11   by these lines or close to these lines pay the price.
